title: Inverse image along a cartesian open refinement is supported on the open
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For any scheme T put Lambda_T = p_T^* Lambda and use module objects over Lambda_T [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let i : X -> Z and i1 : X -> Z1 be open immersions and h : Z -> Z1 such that the square with top id_X, left i, bottom i1 and right h is cartesian. For the underived module inverse image and extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], there exists a natural isomorphism h^* i1_! isomorphic to i_!. There are no properness, quasi-compactness, constructibility, characteristic or boundedness assumptions.

proof.text: The coefficient comparison alpha_j is invertible. The unit for abelian open extension is invertible by full faithfulness; forgetting the module action identifies the unit of linear module open extension with it. Restriction of scalars along alpha_j is an equivalence. Hence the module open-extension unit is invertible and module open extension is fully faithful. The open adjunction units are invertible by the existing private openUnitIsIso helper in Sheaf.Paper.CondensedOpenClosedRecollement, accessed with import all; its proof is reused.

source.place: (1) Exact open operations and the derived adjunction; invertible open unit

proof.text: For F = h^* i1_!, forgetting modules commutes with h^*, after replacing extension of scalars by the inverse of scalar restriction. Apply abelian open base change to the square. Its value shows that the underlying abelian sheaf of F(M) lies in the essential image of i_!. The abelian open counit at that sheaf is therefore invertible. Forgetting the linear module counit gives this same counit; the scalar equivalence then shows that F(M) lies in the essential image of module i_!. Thus the module i-counit is invertible at every F(M).

source.place: The restriction to X; cartesian support and coefficient transport

proof.text: Insert the invertible i1-unit, transport the equality i followed by h = i1 through the pullback-composition isomorphism, and contract the i-counit at F. Each factor is invertible by the preceding steps, naturally in M. Their composite is an isomorphism i_! -> F; invert it to obtain the stated natural isomorphism. Empty opens and identity refinements satisfy the same argument.
